title: Whole recut upscaled 3x — the calibrated pipeline, run end to end on a real delivery
summary: The calibrated '1.5x restore + local upscale to size' pipeline, run on the 22.2s six-shot recut: all 532 frames in one pass, 2016×2688 final cut in 7 minutes. A 3x direct probe on the same clip measured 13.3s/frame — the full clip would need about 2 hours, for only a half-notch more sharpness.

items.label: Face 3-way compare left: stretched source / middle: 1.5x + local upscale (final pipeline) / right: 3x direct probe — all three match on expression, no face change on this clip ★
Full-frame 3-way compare lace, hem edges and fabric folds get sharper step by step

stats: Last round's calibration (red line: 1.5x) stopped at a 5s clip. This time we ran the finalized pipeline on the 22.2s six-shot recut, whole clip in one pass, to check speed and quality at a real delivery length
2016×2688 (3x the 672×896 source) · 532 frames · with audio · 426.6s on the server + local upscale, about 7 minutes total

48-frame sample measured 639.3s ≈ 13.3s/frame, so the full clip would need about 2 hours; the 3-way face compare shows matching expressions, but sharpness is only a touch better than the 1.5x pipeline

Last round, 3x direct turned one clip's closed-mouth smile into a toothy grin. This clip stayed clean start to finish — face change is not a given, but 13x the compute for a half-notch of sharpness still does not pay off
Face, hair strands, lace and hem edges, and stage-light textures each gain one notch of clarity; for the stretched-source comparison see the full-frame 3-way image
Same as the calibration round: SeedVR2 7B fp8 · 1 step · color correction lab · local lanczos upscale to final size
findings: The finalized pipeline reproduces at 22.2s / 532 frames: zero expression change frame by frame, and the quality gain matches the 5s calibration clip — it can serve as the delivery default as is

Speed rule of thumb, re-calibrated against measurements: a 22.2s clip took 426.6s for the whole thing ≈ 19x its own seconds, inside the calibration round's 'x15~25' band — the scheduling math can stay as is
The real cost of 3x direct is compute, not artifacts: 13.3s/frame vs 0.8s/frame, and the only payoff is marginal sharpness — not worth scheduling unless frame-by-frame acceptance is justified

'Upscaling changes faces' is a probabilistic risk, not a certainty: same model, same ratio, one clip failed and one stayed clean start to finish — so the red line stays at 1.5x by clip category, and one safe run does not loosen it
